card.title: Nintendo Wii Disc Drive Repair

claims.statement: Wii laser pot should be about 600 Ω (especially for dual-layer discs); adjust very slowly—an eighth turn can move it 100 Ω or more.
No red laser light = replace laser; laser not moving = replace stepper motor; a faulty laser can stop the spindle spinning.
GameCube discs not seating/ejecting is usually a bent top drive cover or a seized mechanism.
A dead drive: check power/data connections, inspect the drive board for missing caps or corrosion, then replace the board.

procedure: Check spin, laser light and laser travel.
Replace laser, motor or drive board as indicated.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
